ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BATU BARA REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2016
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public spaces or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
This regional regulation regulates protection efforts for women and child victims of violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and child victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children.

Article 3
The Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to: a. prevent all forms of violence against women and children;
b. protect women and provide services to women and children victims of violence; and
c. empower women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Batu Bara Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Batu Bara.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Child protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a Woman.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
13. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
14. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims covering physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
15. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions naturally.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to the region of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
18. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.
19. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence, covering complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
20. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in reports/providing handling services for complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article 12
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities on the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities on the Protection of Women and Children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities on the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

1.8.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the regulation’s operative provisions define and regulate “kekerasan terhadap perempuan dan anak” (violence against women/children) and service mechanisms for victims of such violence. It does NOT explicitly state that human trafficking is within the scope of violence covered. The judge relied only on the “Mengingat/In View of” legal basis citing UU 21/2007 (trafficking in persons) and PP 9/2008 (integrated services for trafficking victims). A citation in the legal basis does not, by itself, mean the local regulation substantively includes trafficking as a covered form of violence; it can simply be a reference framework. Therefore, the English candidates contained enough context to answer “No” for ‘human trafficking included’, but the judge over-interpreted the legal-basis citation as substantive inclusion.

2.5.translated_snippet: a. coverage of women and children victims of violence who receive complaint handling by trained officers in integrated service units; b. coverage of women and children victims of violence who receive health services by trained health workers at Puskesmas and Hospitals; c. coverage of Social Rehabilitation services provided by trained Social Rehabilitation officers for women and children victims of violence in integrated service units; d. coverage of spiritual guidance services provided by trained spiritual guidance officers for women and children victims of violence in integrated service units;
2.5.evaluator_rationale: The minimum service standards include performance indicators requiring services to be delivered by trained officers/health workers/social rehabilitation officers/spiritual guidance officers, implying training/capacity requirements for service workers.

(1) In implementing Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, the community may:

4.1.rationale: The original Indonesian Article 6(2)(d) requires the community to “memberikan informasi dan/atau melaporkan tindak kekerasan … kepada pihak yang berwenang” (provide information and/or report acts of violence to authorities). This is about reporting incidents, not providing public information/education campaigns to prevent VAW. The regulation’s explicit education/outreach-type provision is in Article 16(1)(b): “melakukan sosialisasi hak Perempuan dan Anak secara mandiri” (conduct socialization of women’s and children’s rights independently), but that is not what the judge cited for 4.1. Since the candidates shown to the judge included Article 6 and Article 16, the judge could have distinguished reporting from prevention education; instead it incorrectly treated reporting as an information/education primary-prevention measure. Therefore the main cause is evaluation_failure.

4.2.translated_snippet: b. conduct socialization of the rights of Women and Children independently; b. justice and gender equality;
4.2.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly references gender equality as a guiding principle and includes community participation through socialization of the rights of women and children, which aligns with information/education on women’s rights and gender equality.
